/* Per-button action cooldowns persist across redraws. The handler guard also
   rejects synthetic/keyboard clicks; these styles make the remaining wait clear. */
.act-action { cursor:pointer; }
.act-cooldown, .pbtn-cooldown { pointer-events:none; cursor:wait; opacity:.58; }
.act-cooldown .act-cost { color:#a2402f; font-weight:bold; }
.pbtn-cooldown .pbtn-text { color:#a2402f; font-weight:bold; }

</style>
</head>

<body>

<div id="game-shell">
<div id="taskbar"></div>
<div id="taskbar-controls"><button id="tab-left" title="Scroll tabs left">&lt;</button><button id="tab-right" title="Scroll tabs right">&gt;</button><button id="tab-home" title="Return to the ship">Home</button></div>
<div id="sidepanel"></div>
<div id="sidefoot"></div>
<div id="content"></div>
<div id="statusbar"></div>
</div>

<script type="text/javascript">
/* ================================================================
  SPACESHIP COMMAND
  An action-driven ship management game in a single offline HTA.
  The original dashboard, rooms and ongoing-task engine are shared
  by the port, contract, incident and persistence systems below.

 ABSOLUTE RULE ALREADY ENFORCED HERE
 The idle screen is free. Nothing on it consumes an action and
 nothing on it advances game state. The only thing that moves is
 cosmetic dot drift, which touches no data the game cares about.

 LANGUAGE CONSTRAINT
 Trident / IE engine. ES5 only. var only, no let or const, no
 arrow functions, no template literals, no promises, no
 Array.forEach / map / indexOf, no classList, no addEventListener
 without fallback. Plain for loops throughout.
 ================================================================ */


/* ================================================================
  SECTION A : SHIP DEFINITION DATA
  Everything the diagram draws is read from these arrays. Adding a
  room later means adding one object here, not editing the render
  code. Geometry is in pixels relative to the hull box.
  ================================================================ */

var LARGE_SHIP = {
   name : "SC Tessellate",
   className: "Kestrel-series light hauler",
   registry : "TX-4471",
   commander: "Commander",
   /* spec sheet - read by the Vessel drop-down in the sidebar */
   built : "2387",
   yard : "Halvan Reach Yards, slip 9",
   refit : "2391 - spine and dorsal pod added",
   length : "212 m",
   beam : "64 m",
   height : "48 m",
   mass : "9,400 t laden",
   decks : "4",
   berths : "14",
   drive : "Twin nacelle, single primary core"
};
var SHIP = {
   name:"SC Wren", className:"Wren-series compact courier", registry:"WN-1083",
   commander:"Commander", built:"2388", yard:"Kessler Cooperative Yards",
   refit:"Compact multipurpose fit", length:"88 m", beam:"28 m", height:"22 m",
   mass:"2,100 t laden", decks:"3", berths:"6", drive:"Single nacelle, compact core"
};

/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
  THE HULL, AS DATA
  A side cross-section of a ship built around a long main body:
  a dorsal spine riding on top, a ventral pod slung underneath,
  two nacelles on stub pylons, and a command lens at the bow.
  Recognisably of the same family as the ships everyone pictures
  when you say starship - and deliberately not one of them: the
  nacelles sit ABOVE and BELOW the axis rather than side by side,
  and the lens is a bow section, not a saucer bolted on a neck.
  Rooms are positioned in STAGE coordinates, not hull-relative,
  because there is no longer one hull to be relative to.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
var HULL = [
   { id:"nac-d", cls:"hp-nacelle", x:140, y:6, w:420, h:30 },
   { id:"pyl-d1", cls:"hp-pylon", x:214, y:36, w:18, h:12 },
   { id:"pyl-d2", cls:"hp-pylon", x:468, y:36, w:18, h:12 },
   { id:"spine", cls:"hp-spine", x:200, y:46, w:580, h:58 },
   { id:"body", cls:"hp-body", x:90, y:102, w:810, h:256 },
   { id:"pod", cls:"hp-pod", x:240, y:358, w:480, h:58 },
   { id:"pyl-v1", cls:"hp-pylon", x:300, y:416, w:18, h:8 },
   { id:"pyl-v2", cls:"hp-pylon", x:642, y:416, w:18, h:8 },
   { id:"nac-v", cls:"hp-nacelle", x:230, y:424, w:420, h:30 },
   { id:"lens", cls:"hp-lens", x:850, y:150, w:290, h:160 }
];

/* Room ids stay stable for saved voyages. The numbered bays
  are fitted with live systems by ROOM_FITS below. */
var ROOMS = [
   /* --- MAIN DECK A ------------------------------------- */
   { id:"engine", name:"Engine Room", x:100, y:112, w:160, h:94,

  systems:"Propulsion / Power", tag:"AFT", tone:"#f4efe6" },
  { id:"o2", name:"O2 Filter Room", x:268, y:112, w:126, h:94,
   systems:"Life support - filters and canister rack",
   tag:"DECK A", tone:"#f4efe6" },
  { id:"quarters", name:"Crew Quarters", x:402, y:112, w:130, h:94,
   systems:"Habitation - shared bunks", tag:"DECK A", tone:"#faf7f2" },
  { id:"mess", name:"Mess Hall", x:540, y:112, w:142, h:94,
   systems:"Galley / Rations", tag:"DECK A", tone:"#faf7f2" },
  { id:"r1", name:"Medical Bay", x:690, y:112, w:150, h:94,
   systems:"Triage / treatment", tag:"DECK A", tone:"#fdfbf7" },

  /* --- MAIN DECK B ------------------------------------- */
  { id:"cargo", name:"Cargo Hold", x:100, y:240, w:308, h:94,
   systems:"Storage - 3 bays", tag:"DECK B", tone:"#f4efe6" },
  { id:"science", name:"Science Room", x:416, y:240, w:160, h:94,
   systems:"Survey records / scan logs", tag:"DECK B", tone:"#faf7f2" },
  { id:"simulacron", name:"Simulacron Core", x:584, y:240, w:90, h:94,
   systems:"Memory / dreams", tag:"DECK B", tone:"#f7efe9" },
  { id:"r2", name:"Workshop", x:682, y:240, w:158, h:94,
   systems:"Salvage / repair kits", tag:"DECK B", tone:"#fdfbf7" },

  /* --- DORSAL SPINE ------------------------------------ */
  { id:"r3", name:"Sensor Array", x:206, y:54, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Sensor calibration", tag:"SPINE", tone:"#faf7f2" },
  { id:"r4", name:"Comms Relay", x:320, y:54, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Local traffic / signals", tag:"SPINE", tone:"#fdfbf7" },
  { id:"r5", name:"Thermal Control", x:434, y:54, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Drive cooling", tag:"SPINE", tone:"#faf7f2" },
  { id:"r6", name:"Power Bus", x:548, y:54, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Emergency distribution", tag:"SPINE", tone:"#fdfbf7" },
  { id:"r7", name:"Shield Array", x:662, y:54, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Power / shield transfer", tag:"SPINE", tone:"#faf7f2" },

  /* --- VENTRAL POD ------------------------------------- */
  { id:"r8", name:"Hydroponics", x:252, y:366, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Produce / rations", tag:"POD", tone:"#faf7f2" },
  { id:"r9", name:"Recyclers", x:366, y:366, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Salvage / O2 canisters", tag:"POD", tone:"#fdfbf7" },
  { id:"r10", name:"Fuel Reserve", x:480, y:366, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Salvage / fuel cells", tag:"POD", tone:"#faf7f2" },
  { id:"r11", name:"Damage Control", x:594, y:366, w:106, h:44, small:true,
   systems:"Emergency hull patching", tag:"POD", tone:"#fdfbf7" },

  /* --- COMMAND LENS -----------------------------------
    The lens is an ELLIPSE, so a room near its top or bottom
    must be short AND narrow or its corners hang outside the
    curve. Checked corner by corner against the ellipse. */
  { id:"r12", name:"Observation", x:940, y:160, w:110, h:32, small:true,
   systems:"Local survey / history", tag:"LENS", tone:"#fdfbf7" },
  { id:"bridge", name:"Bridge", x:890, y:196, w:210, h:68,
   systems:"Navigation / Comms", tag:"FWD", tone:"#f7f2e9" },
  { id:"r13", name:"Recreation", x:940, y:268, w:110, h:32, small:true,
   systems:"Crew relationships", tag:"LENS", tone:"#fdfbf7" }
];
var CORRIDOR = { x:100, y:210, w:740, h:26 };

/* Each bay gets its own visual language as well as a working system.
   The small glyphs fit into the deck plan; the richer room card is
   used by facilities that do not already have a dedicated machine view. */
var ROOM_SCENES = {
  engine:{glyph:"reactor", code:"PROPULSION / 01", label:"Primary drive manifold", description:"Twin coolant loops feed the compact core.", accent:"#d18a4c"},
  o2:{glyph:"filter", code:"LIFE SUPPORT / 02", label:"Atmosphere recovery", description:"Three canisters scrub and recirculate cabin air.", accent:"#42aaa3"},
  quarters:{glyph:"habitat", code:"HABITAT / 03", label:"Crew quarters", description:"Six berths, lockers and a shared watch board.", accent:"#b59670"},
  mess:{glyph:"habitat", code:"GALLEY / 04", label:"Rations and meal prep", description:"The rack, stove and water line share one counter.", accent:"#d3a257"},
  r1:{glyph:"medical", code:"MEDICAL / 05", label:"Triage and treatment", description:"A compact care station with monitored recovery beds.", accent:"#d66d71"},
  cargo:{glyph:"cargo", code:"STORES / 06", label:"Cargo and salvage", description:"Three restrained bays keep recovered material secure.", accent:"#83a8c7"},
  science:{glyph:"orbit", code:"SCIENCE / 07", label:"Survey archive", description:"Scans, observations and packaged data are filed here.", accent:"#6ebed4"},
  simulacron:{glyph:"core", code:"SIMULACRON / 08", label:"Memory mosaic", description:"A quiet core turns lived experience into insight.", accent:"#a981d0"},
  r2:{glyph:"cargo", code:"WORKSHOP / 09", label:"Fabrication bench", description:"Recovered alloys become tools and repair kits.", accent:"#ce9564"},
  r3:{glyph:"orbit", code:"SENSORS / 10", label:"Long-range aperture", description:"The array calibrates one scan at a time.", accent:"#55c3d6"},
  r4:{glyph:"network", code:"COMMS / 11", label:"Relay and signal desk", description:"Local traffic and old transmissions share a receiver.", accent:"#78a9e8"},
  r5:{glyph:"reactor", code:"THERMAL / 12", label:"Radiator control", description:"Heat exchangers protect the worn drive.", accent:"#e37e57"},
  r6:{glyph:"reactor", code:"POWER / 13", label:"Emergency distribution", description:"A protected bus routes power between systems.", accent:"#e0b85e"},
  r7:{glyph:"network", code:"DEFENCE / 14", label:"Shield harmonics", description:"The array trades reserve power for protection.", accent:"#6d9fc6"},
  r8:{glyph:"garden", code:"HYDROPONICS / 15", label:"Grow beds", description:"Produce can be turned into fresh shipboard rations.", accent:"#7daf69"},
  r9:{glyph:"filter", code:"RECYCLING / 16", label:"Material recovery", description:"Salvage is separated into useful life-support stock.", accent:"#69b88a"},
  r10:{glyph:"cargo", code:"FUEL RESERVE / 17", label:"Cell refinery", description:"A small press recovers one fuel cell from salvage.", accent:"#d39a51"},
  r11:{glyph:"cargo", code:"DAMAGE CONTROL / 18", label:"Hull patch station", description:"Brace plates are cut to fit the damaged section.", accent:"#d56d5d"},
  r12:{glyph:"orbit", code:"OBSERVATION / 19", label:"External survey port", description:"A clear forward window records each place once.", accent:"#80c8d5"},
  bridge:{glyph:"network", code:"COMMAND / 20", label:"Flight and watch control", description:"Navigation, crew status and the ship's working board.", accent:"#dfb85e"},
  r13:{glyph:"habitat", code:"RECREATION / 21", label:"Common room", description:"Two crew can share a meal and repair a strained bond.", accent:"#c68eb4"}
};

/* Four starting crew, scrappy and not yet experts. Their needs,
  assignments, pay and training are live state.

  OWNERSHIP, SPELLED OUT SO IT CANNOT DRIFT: STATE.shiplets is the
  Purse - the SHIP's money. c.wallet is the Wallet - the PERSON's
  money, never shared with any other crew member. The two pools
  must never share a name or a variable. tickPayroll() is the
  ONLY function allowed to write to c.wallet (it credits the same
  wage it subtracts from STATE.shiplets, finishing a transfer that
  used to just vanish). Nothing else may touch it until a reason
  to spend it - a market, a tavern, a loan - actually exists. */
var CREW = [
   {
      id:"rell", name:"Rell Aventine", role:"Pilot / Navigation",
      room:"bridge", activity:"Bridge watch", colour:"#8c6f4e",
      sex:"f", hair:"#c9a85c", hair2:"#e2c793", skin:"#f2dcc0", hairStyle:"bun",
      health:96, morale:71, fatigue:34, hunger:22, wallet:0,
      /* HUNGER TICK. Counts up to MESS_EVERY (25) actions, this
         crew member's own clock, then they go to the rack. Four
         crew started at once would all want feeding on the exact
         same action - staggered so a steady trickle of meals
         happens instead, a quarter of the cycle apart each. A
         new hire later simply starts at 0 on the action they
         join, which staggers itself for free. */
      hungerTick:0,
      traits:"Steady, quietly stubborn",
      /* BIOGRAPHICAL - static record fields, not computed, but
         still real: set once here and read from here, never
         invented at render time. Homeworlds are drawn from the
         sector chart (SECTOR_BODIES) so a crew member's past and
         the nav map agree with each other. */
      race:"Human", age:41, homeworld:"Orrin Gate",
      hobby:"Plots old trade routes by hand, for the quiet of it",
      religion:"The Driftwatch (quietly devout)"
   },
   {
      id:"jax", name:"Jax Moreno", role:"Engineer",
      room:"engine", activity:"Inspecting coolant line", colour:"#b05a42",
      sex:"m", hair:"#5c4436", hair2:"#7d6049", skin:"#d2a781", hairStyle:"cowlick",
      health:88, morale:64, fatigue:52, hunger:41, wallet:20,
      hungerTick:6,
      traits:"Blunt, fixes things twice",
      race:"Human", age:35, homeworld:"Vance Cluster",
      hobby:"Strips down obsolete engine parts and rebuilds them better",
      religion:"None",
      /* JOB ASSIGNMENT. A crew member holding the maintenance job
        services the drive on his own initiative - but only once
        condition has fallen to jobAt. An untrained hand leaves it
        far too late. Training at a station, or hiring a better
        engineer, raises jobAt. Assigning the job will be done in
        the crew member's own task window. */
          job:"maintenance", skill:"Untrained", jobAt:30
     },
     {
          id:"bo", name:"Bo Ferreira", role:"Life Support",
          room:"o2", activity:"Checking the canister rack", colour:"#c08a3e",
          sex:"m", hair:"#8a857e", hair2:"#a8a39c", skin:"#c69070", hairStyle:"thin",
          health:91, morale:69, fatigue:37, hunger:28, wallet:30,
          hungerTick:13,
          traits:"Methodical, hoards spares",
          race:"Human", age:47, homeworld:"Bryce Anchorage",
          hobby:"Catalogues every spare part on the ship by hand",
          religion:"The Driftwatch (devout)",
          /* JOB ASSIGNMENT - the second one in the game.
            jobAt is read by the JOB, not by the engine: for the
            maintenance job it is a condition percentage, for the
            filter job it is an AIR STAGE (4 clean .. 0 foul). An
            untrained hand waits for stage 1 - BAD - which means
            the crew have already been labouring for ten actions
            before he thinks to do anything about it. Training, or
            a better technician, raises that to 3 or 2. */
          job:"filters", skill:"Untrained", jobAt:1
     },
     {
          id:"suri", name:"Suri Tal", role:"General Duties",
          room:"mess", activity:"Preparing rations", colour:"#7f9161",
          sex:"f", hair:"#2f2a26", hair2:"#4a423b", skin:"#e8c8a4", hairStyle:"long",
          health:93, morale:78, fatigue:28, hunger:15, wallet:0,
          hungerTick:19,
          traits:"Cheerful, notices small things",
          race:"Human", age:26, homeworld:"Kessler System",
          hobby:"Keeps a tin of pressed flowers from every port",
          religion:"The Driftwatch (casual)",
          /* JOB ASSIGNMENT - the third. She was already standing in
            the galley with an activity line that said "Preparing
            rations" before the job existed to back it up - this
            just makes that true. */
          job:"kitchen", skill:"Untrained", jobAt:1
     }
];

/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
   EVENTS - what the ship has noticed but nobody has looked at yet.
   The sidebar shows the KIND and nothing else. Details, choices
   and escalation live in the event task window. The definitions
   are in INCIDENT_TYPES; this array holds active instances.
   ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
var EVENTS = []; /* live incident instances; definitions are in Section M */

/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
  THE PRICE LIST IS THE COMMANDER'S, NOT MINE.
  Ordered 2026-09-30, verbatim:
    "more jobs that cost lest actions to get, cleaner cost one
     actions, engineer cost 2 actions, Navigation 3 actions,
     Filter 3 actions"
    "as more important the work is as more it will cost"
    "Send to DOC: cost 1 actions but be aware he might not come
     back for 7 actions"
    "Learn and train: depends on what and where, online cost
     less than direclty in a spacestaion ... learning
      engineering cost more than learning cleaning"
     "Fire. yeah, that one cost 5 actions."
   These figures are not to be re-based, rounded, merged or
   "simplified" as a side effect of fixing something else. An
   order costs what it says here, and the time it takes to carry
   out is that same number - ONE number per order, so the sheet
   can never again show a price and a duration that disagree.
   The medical bay is the single exception: 1 action to send
   them, DOC_AWAY actions before they are back.
   ----------------------------------------------------------------
   JOBS AND ORDERS
   A job is a standing assignment a crew member acts on by
   himself. jobAt is read BY THE JOB: a condition percentage for
   maintenance, an air stage for filters. trainStep/trainCap say
   what a session of training is worth and where it stops.
   cloth/dark are what the sprite in the quarters wears.
   ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
var JOBS = [
    { id:"",         label:"None",          unique:false, cost:1, wage:0,
      learnOn:0, learnSt:0, feeOn:0, feeSt:0, trainStep:0, trainCap:0, unit:"",
      cloth:"#a2947f", dark:"#857a68" },
    { id:"cleaner", label:"Cleaner", unique:false, cost:1, wage:5,
      learnOn:1, learnSt:2, feeOn:10, feeSt:20, trainStep:1, trainCap:5, unit:"",
      cloth:"#7f9161", dark:"#66754d" },
    { id:"maintenance", label:"Engineer", unique:true, cost:2, wage:10,
      learnOn:3, learnSt:5, feeOn:30, feeSt:50, trainStep:15, trainCap:75, unit:"%",
      cloth:"#b05a42", dark:"#8f4735" },
    { id:"navigation", label:"Navigation", unique:true, cost:3, wage:15,
      learnOn:4, learnSt:6, feeOn:40, feeSt:60, trainStep:1, trainCap:5, unit:"",
      cloth:"#8c6f4e", dark:"#6b5338" },
    { id:"filters", label:"Filters", unique:true, cost:3, wage:15,
      learnOn:4, learnSt:6, feeOn:40, feeSt:60, trainStep:1, trainCap:3, unit:" air",
      cloth:"#c08a3e", dark:"#9c6f2f" },
    { id:"kitchen", label:"Cook", unique:true, cost:3, wage:15,
      learnOn:4, learnSt:6, feeOn:40, feeSt:60, trainStep:1, trainCap:3,
      unit:" ration/action",
      cloth:"#d2a059", dark:"#a67f3f" }
];
/* THE PRICE IS THE POINT. A cleaner is a word and a mop; an
   engineer is a week of somebody's attention; navigation, life
   support and the galley are the jobs that cost people their
   health when they are done badly, so they cost the most to
   hand over and the most to teach. Nothing here is free - the
   bill simply arrives at the bottom of the screen instead of at
   the click. */
var ORDERS = [
    { id:"doc", label:"Send to Doc", note:"away up to 7 actions" },
    { id:"learnOn", label:"Learn - aboard", note:"cheap, one step" },
    { id:"learnSt", label:"Learn - station", note:"two steps, needs a dock" },
    { id:"fire", label:"Lay off",            note:"off the payroll, stays aboard" },
    { id:"rest", label:"Rest",               note:"recover fatigue and morale" }
];
/* An order's price is also how
 long the sheet takes to carry
   out: the bottom button counts the lot down as one bar, and
   nobody takes new orders until it is empty. Giving the order
   costs the commander one action, like every other button.
   The medical bay is the exception - it keeps a body for
  DOC_AWAY actions AFTER the sheet is finished. */
var DOC_AWAY = 7;

/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
  PAYROLL
  A job is not a favour - the hand holding it draws a wage, and
  the wage is the job's own price times five. Nobody unemployed
  costs anything, and nobody unemployed does anything either:
  that is the whole bargain. Payday lands every PAY.every
  actions, measured on the same counter as everything else.
  If the purse cannot cover the bill the ship pays DOWN the list,
  dearest first - life support and navigation keep the crew
  alive, the cleaner is what a short captain stops paying for -
  and anyone left unpaid comes off the payroll on the spot.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
var PAY = {
   every : 100, /* actions between paydays */
   hit : 12 /* morale lost by a hand nobody could pay */
};
    /* changing a job */

/* Hull-exterior stat readouts - manifesto 1.5. All right-clickable. */
var STATS = [
   { id:"hull", label:"Hull Integrity", value:100, unit:"%", colour:"#7f9161" },
   { id:"shield", label:"Shields",     value:62, unit:"%", colour:"#c08a3e" },
   { id:"energy", label:"Energy",        value:88, unit:"%", colour:"#7f9161" },
   { id:"fuel", label:"Fuel",        value:74, unit:"%", colour:"#8c6f4e" }
];

var INFOS = [
   { id:"location", label:"Current Location", value:"Kessler Drift - open space" },
   { id:"contacts", label:"Nearby Objects", value:"No contacts in scan range" },
   { id:"life", label:"Life Support", value:"Nominal - atmosphere stable" }
];

/* A resource line is either a plain value or DERIVED from one of
   the stores below. Derived lines cannot drift out of step with
   the room that holds the stuff - there is one copy of the truth
   and the sidebar reads it. */
var RESOURCES = [
    { label:"Shiplets", from:"purse" },
    { label:"Fuel cells", from:"fuelCells" },
    { label:"Rations", from:"rations" },
    { label:"Repair kits", from:"repairKits" },
    { label:"Medkits", from:"medkits" },
    { label:"O2 tanks", from:"o2" },
    { label:"Goods",      from:"goods" },
    { label:"Survey data", from:"survey" }
];

/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
  STORE 1 : OXYGEN                          (lives in the O2 Filter Room)
  Canisters are the stock; filters are what actually breathes for
  the crew. A filter loses charge slowly as actions are spent
  anywhere on the ship, and a canister has to be carried over and
  loaded into it BY HAND. Nothing here is automatic - that is the
  point of the room.
  The drain itself belongs to the event/economy phase; the data
  and the room are seeded here so it has somewhere to land.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
var LIFE = {
   canisters : 6,
   capacity : 10,
   /* THREE SLOTS, THREE STATES.
      empty - nothing seated, the air gets no help
      installed - a canister is in and the machine is ready
      active - the machine is running on it
      A canister leaves the rack the moment an install is
      COMMITTED, not when it finishes: it is in the player's
      hands from that point on. */
   slots : [
       { id:"s0", name:"Slot 1", state:"empty" },
       { id:"s1", name:"Slot 2", state:"empty" },
       { id:"s2", name:"Slot 3", state:"empty" }
   ],
   lifeMax : 200, /* a full charge, in actions */
   decay : 4          /* lost per action spent anywhere aboard */
};

/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
  THE AIR ITSELF
  When the bank dies the cabin does not go foul on the spot - the
  air already in the room holds for a while and then declines in
  four visible steps, five actions each. Twenty actions from a
  dead bank to unbreathable.
  EVERYTHING BAD AIR DOES IS IN THIS ONE TABLE. Index is the
  stage: 4 is clean, 0 is foul. A future effect - fatigue, morale,
  a medical event - is another column here, not a new branch
  somewhere in the engine.
    slow : multiplier on work done BY THE CREW. The commander
            is not slowed; he is the one giving the orders and
            he can hold his breath. Crew work takes longer.
    jobDrop : how far a crew member's own trigger threshold
            slips. An engineer who waits for 30% waits for
            20% when the air is bad - he is slower to notice
            and slower to care.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
var AIR = {
   holdMax : 20, /* actions of breathable air after the bank dies */
   step : 5 /* actions per step of decline                        */
};
var AIR_STAGES = [
   { word:"FOUL", tone:"#b05a42", slow:2.00, jobDrop:10, harm:5 }, /* 0 */
   { word:"BAD", tone:"#b05a42", slow:1.50, jobDrop:10, harm:10 }, /* 1 */
   { word:"THIN", tone:"#c08a3e", slow:1.25, jobDrop:5, harm:0 }, /* 2 */
